content.title: Contact-Triggered Energy | Physical Impact Before Transient Feedback
content.summary: Establish one original clearly adult fighter, readable opponents and a stable combat geography before spectacle grows. Every decisive beat must follow the same causal order: an adult commits a visible physical trajectory, bodies or a prop make real contact, and only then a brief bounded energy, dust, hair, fabric or light reaction appears at the contact point. Keep the reaction shorter than the initiating action and preserve silhouettes throughout. Escalate through opponent count and reaction radius rather than pre-emptive projectiles. End by stopping all effects and holding the same adult in the established space.

quick_start.input_format: Show one clearly adult original fighter, opponents and a stable ground relation before the first effect. + Require a visible committed trajectory and real contact before every energy reaction. + Keep every reaction bounded to the contact point and shorter than the initiating action. + Escalate opponent count and reaction radius while keeping silhouettes and positions legible. + Stop all effects and hold the same adult in the established space after the final exchange.
quick_start.recommended_input: Open in an original shipyard service bay: a clearly adult cobalt-jacket mechanic faces one malfunctioning yellow robotic arm on a marked floor lane; the arm swings, the mechanic blocks with a steel wrench, and only after metal contact a brief amber arc and bolt vibration appear. Each arm commits one readable clamp or sweep before the mechanic redirects it; every metal contact receives one short local amber arc, cable shake and dust response, never a pre-emptive energy attack. After the final wrench block, all arcs stop. Hold the same adult alone on the marked lane as cables settle and service lights return to a steady baseline; no text or brand.

creative_dna.mechanism: Establish one original clearly adult fighter, readable opponents and a stable combat geography before spectacle grows. Every decisive beat must follow the same causal order: an adult commits a visible physical trajectory, bodies or a prop make real contact, and only then a brief bounded energy, dust, hair, fabric or light reaction appears at the contact point. Keep the reaction shorter than the initiating action and preserve silhouettes throughout. Escalate through opponent count and reaction radius rather than pre-emptive projectiles. End by stopping all effects and holding the same adult in the established space. The reusable mechanism is physical action first, contact proof second, transient multimodal feedback third, controlled escalation and quiet reset—not the source people, gym, costumes, choreography, exact discharge design, creator identity or timing.

invariants.ablation_failure: Without the baseline, later light could be mistaken for the cause of motion.

invariants.purpose: Raises intensity without abandoning the combat grammar.

anti_copy_exclusions: source woman, surrounding men, faces, bodies and gym clothing
source training hall, windows, floor and exact sunlight
source punches, kicks, blocks, falls and exact choreography
source white-blue discharge shape, dust density and lighting pulses
source camera path, timing, creator identity and Seedance 2.5 wording
